Text.Text: Look at that turn. You carry the eye with you now -- the students copy your footwork when they think I'm not watching. The halls are open, the form has a center again, and I have nothing left to teach you that the staff won't say better.

Keep walking, I don't stop between forms. Your grip says staff; your feet say the staff is still two blades to you. Finish that education first. When it stops being two blades and starts being one motion -- when there's nothing left of the discipline you haven't made your own -- come find me about the cyclone.

Walk with me -- I think better moving. You came for the cyclone, and you're about to say you're ready, so I'll finish the sentence: you're ready to start. The trial halls under this enclave are full of students spinning the form with no center, and their masters won't intervene. I will, through you. Go down into the Dantooine Jedi Enclave Trial Halls, defeat six of the adepts, and bring me the Saber Cyclone Enclave Trial Slate they drill from. Their bad orbit starts on that slate.

Then keep up. The key I've just put in your hand opens the sealed door on the enclave's lower ring. Six adepts, the slate, back to me before your sweat dries. And watch their turns while you break them -- even a wrong lesson teaches.

Most forms plant their feet and swing. The cyclone never plants. The staff keeps turning -- every parry feeds the next arc, defense becomes orbit, and whatever steps into the orbit gets carried out of it. What they're doing down there is all spin and no center. You'll learn the difference by unmaking theirs.

Below us. The enclave sealed the lower trial halls when the drills turned bloody -- the door is on the lower ring, past the meditation court, and the key I'll give you when you take the work opens the seal. Once you're through, stay in the halls. Everything past that door considers itself part of the trial.

Adepts who've drilled the cyclone's opening turns until they're reflex. Reflex without judgment cuts in both directions -- they won't stop at first blood, because nobody taught them where a drill ends. Don't extend your arcs to impress them. Six, cleanly, and out.
You still owe the lower halls six adepts, and I still want the Saber Cyclone Enclave Trial Slate they drill from. Walk with me later -- right now the only conversation you owe is down there.
There -- your arcs came back shorter. The halls did that in a day; imagine a year. And that's the slate under your arm. Hand it over.

Six adepts and their drill slate. Want to know what's wrong with it? Nothing. Every form on it is copied perfectly -- that's the lesson. Perfect copies, no center. The credits are for your time. The next turn is faster.

Fall in beside me -- colonnade pace. The adepts were students; the specialists are the ones teaching them. Five of them run focus drills in the deep chambers, and they've hung the whole practice on a kyber shard that should never have left the vaults. Take the five apart and bring me the Saber Cyclone Kyber Focus Shard before it teaches anyone else to spin blind.

Quick answer. I like that better than a careful one. Deep chambers, five specialists, and the shard comes back wrapped -- kyber listens, and I don't want it learning anything on the way. If you catch yourself matching their rhythm, break your own first.

Kyber holds a note when you feed it attention. The specialists use the shard as a false center -- focus on the stone and the cyclone feels effortless, right up until the stone isn't there. It's a crutch dressed as a doctrine. That's why it comes out of the halls and into my hand.

Same door on the lower ring -- your key still turns the seal. The specialists keep past the chambers where you met the adepts, deeper in. You'll hear them before you see them; kyber hums when it's working, and theirs never rests.

Better than the adepts, and worse. The shard smooths their gaps, so they're flawless until you break their tempo -- then they stumble over their own orbit. Change your speed and keep changing it. And they spar live steel down there, so treat every exchange as real. It is.
Five specialists, deep chambers, and the Saber Cyclone Kyber Focus Shard comes home with you. Nothing about the assignment has changed while you stood here -- except how long it's been waiting.
I can hear it from here. Even wrapped, that shard hums like it's mid-drill. You outlasted five teachers at their own tempo -- give it over.

Listen to it. Kyber sings whatever you feed it, and they fed it certainty for a year. You heard the difference; they never did. Take your pay, walk the long way back, and let your arms argue about what they learned.

Stop. Don't fall in beside me this time -- stand still, because this I say once. The trial ring below has a warden. He proctored these halls for twenty years, and when the cyclone drills turned bad he didn't end them; he started keeping score. Now he holds the ring, wears a sigil he cracked with his own grading hand, and he has flung stronger blades than yours out of the ring for interrupting his orbit. Bring two blades you trust -- that's instruction, not advice. Put him down and bring me the Saber Cyclone Fractured Trial Sigil.

Then hear the rest at walking pace. He fights the ring like it's his orbit, because it is -- don't take turns with him. Overlap him: one draws the arc, one breaks it, one finishes. That's why you're bringing company. Sigil off his belt, and come back standing.

He graded my students for twenty years. He graded me, once -- passed me, which I've held against him ever since. Somewhere in the scoring he stopped seeing duelists and started seeing gaps. Whatever he says to you mid-fight, don't answer. He's counting the syllables you waste.

Through your usual door, past the deep chambers, down to the trial ring itself. He's sealed it from inside, but the seal answers the key you already carry -- he wants challengers. He just wants them tired when they arrive. Don't oblige him. Go rested, go fed, go three.

A cyclone with twenty years of patience at its center. He doesn't tire, he doesn't chase, and every solo challenge the students sent him ended the same way. Alone, you're a lesson he's already graded. Three of you are a problem he hasn't -- so bring the problem.
The warden still holds the trial ring, and the Saber Cyclone Fractured Trial Sigil still hangs off his belt. If you're waiting on your blades to arrive, good. That's the assignment working.
You walked back up the stairs -- I know because the students stopped whispering about the ring an hour ago. Sigil first. Then breathe.

Cracked down the middle. He did that himself the day he decided his orbit was the standard everything else fell short of. I'll set it back where the masters' mark belongs, crack and all -- some lessons should stay visible. You did this the right way: not alone. Keep that shape. You'll need it once more.

Walk with me -- you've earned the fast pace. With the warden gone, his inner circle has no one left to grade them, and it's made them honest at last: four duelists barricaded in the council chamber, because the form is all they have left to hold. They keep the council's trial chit among them like it's a title. It isn't. Take all four down and bring me the Saber Cyclone Council Trial Chit -- the council wants it back before they'll reopen the halls.

Good. One more thing, between strides: don't let them make it four duels. It's one fight with four parts -- treat it that way and you're back by nightfall. The chit comes straight to me; the council counts hours now.

The warden's chosen -- the four he scored highest. Each one built their cyclone around a different lie: speed, reach, endurance, fury. Together they cover one another's gaps, which is the only true thing he ever taught them.
The council chamber, one hall past the trial ring you cleared -- same key, same stairs, further in. They know the ring fell. They'll be waiting, which spares you the trouble of looking.

Four cyclones that learned to orbit each other. Split them if you can. If you can't, bring enough blades that splitting stops mattering. And watch the one who hangs back -- the warden always graded patience highest.

Four of the inner circle still hold the council chamber, and the Saber Cyclone Council Trial Chit is still in their keeping. The council keeps asking me questions I'd rather answer with the chit in my hand.
The chamber went quiet yesterday -- the whole enclave felt it. You're carrying the chit like it's heavier than it looks. It is. Give it here.

Sealed and unspent. They held the council's proof for a year and never once earned the right to open it. You've earned it four times over. The halls reopen, the council owes me a favor, and I lose my best excuse for walking fast. One trial left -- and I've been avoiding saying her name.

No drill today. Stand with me a moment -- I don't ask that often. The master in the deep hall: I trained her. I gave her the cyclone the way it was given to me, and she took it somewhere I couldn't follow -- an orbit with no center at all, no self left inside the turn. She holds the deepest hall, and she wields the finished form you came here to earn. No one walks out of her circle alone; I've read every report that says so. Take two partners who can hold the turn beside you and end the lesson I couldn't. There's nothing to carry back. Her defeat is the proof, and I'll feel it from up here.

Then the last part, plainly, standing still: her orbit widens as she tires. Most people back away from it -- that's when she takes them. Step in when everyone else would step out. That's the whole secret, and it took me twenty years and one empty chair to learn it. Come back, and I'll finish your sentence one last time.

She was the best center I ever saw. Still, kind, certain -- then the turning became the center, and the rest of her went into it. What's down there remembers every form and none of the reasons. If she speaks, it will sound like me on my best day. It isn't me. It's the form, talking to itself.

The deepest hall, below the council chamber -- the one built for masters' trials, never meant to be sealed. Your key carries anyone who has cleared the ring and the chamber; her door opens to that and nothing else. She knows the halls above have gone quiet. She's waiting for whoever quieted them.

The cyclone as I'll never teach it. Both blades always in motion, nothing wasted, nothing spared -- the very turn you're trying to earn, sharpened by years alone in the dark. A cyclone alone just digs its own crater. Hers is deep. Don't step into it with fewer than three.
She's still in the deep hall. I'd know the moment that changed -- so would every stone in this enclave. Gather your blades. Don't come walk with me again until it's done; I'll only slow you down.
The halls are quiet all the way to the bottom. I walked down to the ring this morning just to listen. I know already -- say it anyway. I want the words.

Then it's yours. The whole turn -- defense into orbit, orbit into stillness. She'd have been proud of how you did it: with others, and not for the spin. I have no trials left for you. Go correct somebody's footing; I hear it's how the best of us start. Me? I finally feel like standing still.
Keep walking. Tell me the trial again.
Six adepts and the slate. Point me at the stairs.
What is the cyclone, exactly?
Where do I find these adepts?
What am I walking into?
Not yet. My footing isn't there.
The Saber Cyclone Enclave Trial Slate. Take it.
Slow down -- the specialists. Go over it again.
Five specialists. The shard comes back with me.
What does the shard actually do?
Where do the specialists train?
How do they fight?
Not this turn. Give me a day.
The Saber Cyclone Kyber Focus Shard. It hasn't stopped humming.
Say the assignment again. All of it.
I'll bring the blades. The warden falls.
Who is this warden?
Where is the trial ring?
What will he throw at us?
My blades aren't here yet. Soon.
The Saber Cyclone Fractured Trial Sigil. The ring is open.
Back to the four. I'm listening.
Four duelists, one chit. Done.
Who are the inner circle?
Where are they holed up?
How do the four fight together?
When my edge comes back. Not before.
The Saber Cyclone Council Trial Chit. The chamber is quiet.
Start over. I want to hear all of it again.
We go together, three of us. It ends there.
What did she become?
Where does she wait?
What should we expect from her?
Not until my people are ready. She can wait.
She's defeated. The cyclone has a center again.
